terminal.description: A shell in your workspace where the demo runs a few operations on each of your caches.

tasks.title: LRU cache in O(1)
tasks.description:
Implement the `LRUCache<K, V>` class in `src/lru.ts`. `new LRUCache(capacity)` holds at most `capacity` entries.

- `get(key)` returns the value or `undefined`. A hit makes the key the most recently used.
- `set(key, value)` adds or replaces and makes the key the most recently used. If that leaves more than `capacity` entries, remove the least recently used.
- `has(key)` does not change the order. `delete(key)` returns whether the key was there.
- `size` is a getter. `keys()` lists keys from least to most recently used.

Every operation except `keys()` must be O(1) on average. The check runs 600,000 operations on a cache of 100,000.
nextSteps: Pick a structure that remembers order and finds keys in O(1).
Write `get` and `set` so both move the key to the recent end.
Evict from the old end when `set` goes over capacity.
Run `node src/demo.ts` and read the first line.
hints: Arrays find keys in O(n). You need lookup by key and an order you can update cheaply. JavaScript has a built-in that gives you both.
A `Map` iterates in insertion order. Deleting a key and setting it again moves it to the end.
The least recently used key is the first one a `Map` iterates: `map.keys().next().value`. Remember that a stored value can be 0, so decide hits with `has`.

tasks.title: Entries that expire
tasks.description:
Implement `TTLCache<K, V>` in `src/ttlCache.ts`: `new TTLCache({ capacity, ttlMs, now })`.

- `set(key, value)` keeps the entry until `now() + ttlMs`. Setting a key again restarts its time.
- An entry is expired once `now()` is at or past that time. Expired entries act as if they are not there for `get`, `has`, `size` and `keys()`.
- `get` on a live entry makes it the most recently used but does not extend its time.
- When `set` adds a new key to a full cache, remove expired entries first. Only if it is still full, evict the least recently used live entry.
- `now` defaults to `Date.now`.
nextSteps: Store `{ value, expiresAt }` for each key.
Write a helper that returns a live entry or removes an expired one.
Use it in `get` and `has`, and sweep expired entries for `size`, `keys()` and a full `set`.
Run the demo and check the second line.
hints: You can reuse the ordering trick from task 1. The new part is a second piece of data per entry.
Never read the time any way other than `this.now()`. The check moves a fake clock between calls.
In `set`, delete the key first, then if the cache is full remove every expired entry, then if it is still full remove the oldest one, then insert.

tasks.title: Entries with a weight
tasks.description:
Implement `WeightedCache<K, V>` in `src/weightedCache.ts`: `new WeightedCache({ maxWeight, onEvict })` limits the total weight instead of the count.

- `set(key, value, weight)` returns `false` and changes nothing when `weight > maxWeight`. Otherwise it adds or replaces the entry, makes it the most recently used, removes least recently used entries until the total is at most `maxWeight`, and returns `true`.
- `onEvict(key, value)` is called for each entry removed to make room, in order. Replacing a key or `delete` does not call it.
- `get`, `has` and `delete` work as in task 1. `size`, `weight` (the total) and `keys()` report the contents.
nextSteps: Store `{ value, weight }` per key and keep a running total.
Handle the too-heavy case first, before touching anything.
Replace, insert, then evict from the old end in a loop while the total is too high.
Run the demo and check the third line.
hints: A running total is cheaper and simpler than adding up every weight each time.
When a key is replaced, its old weight has to come off the total before the new one goes on. `delete` already does that.
Because the new entry fits on its own and is the most recent, a loop that removes the oldest entry while `total > maxWeight` will never remove it.
